text: Your first bath. The water is warm and suspicious. A rubber duck stares at you, judging.
It is 3 a.m. You are hungry. Everyone is asleep. Your stomach growls louder than you can.
A giant finger hovers near your hand. It smells of coffee. Its owner coos and waits.
Someone makes a ridiculous face at you. Cheeks puffed, eyes crossed. They won't stop until you react.
The pacifier fell on the floor. It is a bit fluffy now. The dog has noticed it too.
Tummy time. Your face is in the rug. It smells of feet. A grown-up claps like this is fun.
Diaper emergency. It is up your back somehow. A grown-up approaches with wipes and quiet horror.
A stranger with loud perfume wants to hold you. Big earrings, rustling handbag. Your parent hands you over.
A parent sings to you. Badly. They forget the words and hum the rest. They mean every wrong note.
Your first tooth is coming in. Everything hurts. Your chin is wet with drool. You want to bite the world.
Everyone is waiting for your first word. A phone is filming. A grandparent leans in. Total silence.
You discovered the word "no". It is powerful. Grown-ups freeze when you say it. How far does this go?
Something shiny is across the room. Keys, foil or treasure. The carpet is long. The cat is watching it too.
You crawled into the kitchen. The low cupboard opens. Pots, lids, a whisk. Nobody has seen you yet.
You stand up holding the sofa. Your legs wobble like jelly. A parent holds out their arms. Let go?
The stair gate is left open. The stairs rise like a carpeted mountain. Nobody is looking.
A spoon of green mush approaches, making airplane noises. It smells of peas and lies.
You are in the high chair. The floor is far below. Food makes a lovely splat. The dog waits underneath.
The family pet has a tail. It is right there, swishing, fluffy and warm. The pet is fast asleep.
A new baby came home. Everyone is looking at it. It is small, red and loud. You were here first.
Your sibling has your old rattle. You forgot it existed. Now it is the most important thing ever.
Bedtime. You are not tired. You are very tired. Your eyes keep closing. You refuse to miss anything.
You wanted the blue cup. You got the red cup. Same cup, wrong colour. This is an outrage.
A parent hides behind their hands. They are gone forever. You can hear them breathing in there.
The bath drain gurgles. It wants to eat you. The water slurps toward the hole. Your duck drifts closer.
Someone shows you a tiny plastic toilet. It is bright yellow. They smile too much. What is it for?
You found a crayon. The wall is big, white and empty. Somewhere there is paper. Nobody is watching.
The doctor has a small needle and a big smile. Your parent holds your arm. Everyone says it's quick.
The vacuum is on. It is a monster. It roars, eats crumbs and a sock. Now it is coming your way.
Another toddler is here. They have a better toy. It beeps and flashes. Yours is a wooden spoon.
Hide and seek. You hide behind a curtain. Your feet show. A grown-up loudly wonders where you are.
There is a sock in your mouth. You don't know whose. It tastes of the washing basket. Still chewing.
A baby in the mirror copies everything you do. It pulls your faces. It never says a word.
The checkout has sweets at exactly your eye level. Long queue, tired parent. They already said no once.
A friend only you can see moves in. His name is Gerald. He wears a top hat and wants his own chair.
Somebody drew on the wall. Gerald, probably. The crayon is in your hand, but that proves nothing.
Gerald says he's moving away. He packed a tiny invisible bag. His train leaves from the garden.
First day at daycare. Your parent is edging toward the door. Twelve small strangers stare at you.
Nap time. Everyone is lying down. You are not tired. The mats are lumpy. The kid next to you is awake.
It's bedtime. You need water. And a story. And another water. Your parent sighs in the doorway.
Something in the closet just moved. The door is open a crack. It might be coats. It might not.
There's a pea touching your potatoes. Unacceptable. The pea juice is spreading. This is a crisis.
A green thing is on your fork. Nobody will say what it is. It wobbles. Everyone is watching you.
The big slide. The big kids use it. It is shiny, steep and tall. A big kid zooms down, screaming.
A kid in the sandbox has the good shovel. Red, metal, perfect. Yours is a plastic spoon.
A kid on the swings says you're best friends now. Just like that. They have jam on their face.
Your best friend says you can't come to their pretend castle. It's made of cushions. It still stings.
Your best friend's parent asks if you want to stay the night. Their house creaks. Their cat is huge.
Why is the sky up? Why are feet? Why why why? Your parent takes a very long sip of coffee.
Haircut day. The scissors are very close to your ears. Snip. Cold hair slides down your neck.
Bath time. You have decided you are a fish now. Fish do not need soap. The floor is already wet.
You have to go. But you're SO busy playing. The tower is almost done. You do a small, secret dance.
You want to dress yourself today. Boots, a tutu, a cape and one sock. A grown-up checks the clock.
A baby is coming home. Everyone says you're a big kid now. You never asked. It gets your old blanket.
You painted a picture. It is mostly brown. You mixed every colour. It is either a dog or a feeling.
A grown-up asks you to count to ten in front of everybody. The family goes quiet. Someone is filming.
Your favourite stuffed rabbit is gone. He has one ear and smells like home. Bedtime is coming fast.
A big dog trots over in the park. It is the size of a pony. Its tongue is out. Its tail is going.
You found a beetle. You'd like to keep it. Forever. It is shiny and green. You named it Steve.
Show and tell. You have nothing to show. The kid before you brought a snake skin. Everyone turns.
The class fish needs feeding while the teacher is out. You hold the jar. The fish looks hungry.
A purple crayon looks delicious today. It looks like grape. Nobody is watching the craft table.
A grandparent arrives with pockets full of something. It rustles. Sweets? Tissues? They smell of mints.
The doctor has a needle and a sticker. The sticker is a shiny dinosaur. The needle is a needle.
Everyone has to hold hands and sing a song. The hand on your left is sticky. The teacher claps hard.
You declare the couch a kingdom. You are its ruler. Your crown is a saucepan. Dinner is being called.
Someone's taking the training wheels off your bike. The spanner clinks. The pavement looks hard.
You woke up from a bad dream. The hall is dark. Your heart is racing. Your parents' door looks far.
Your new teacher has a whistle. She uses it indoors. Every blast, somebody drops a pencil.
A front tooth wobbles loose at lunch. It hangs by a thread. Your tongue can't leave it alone.
You read a whole page out loud without stopping. Even the long words. The teacher looks up. So do you.
The kid next to you is eating the glue. Calmly, with a spoon from home. They offer you the pot.
Show and tell is tomorrow. You forgot. Someone is bringing a real lizard. It is already bedtime.
A bigger kid wants your snack. Every day. They wait by the coat pegs, hand out. Today it's your favourite.
The snack kid is back. You have been thinking about this. You practised in the mirror. Their hand is out.
The old snack kid saves you a seat on the bus. They pat the space next to them. They look nervous.
You win a goldfish at the fair. It spins in a plastic bag, looking confused. It needs a name.
Your goldfish is floating upside down. It is not a trick. You tapped the bowl twice. It's gone.
Your homework is unfinished. The dog is right there, chewing a slipper. He already looks guilty.
Last round of the spelling test. The word is very long and has a silent letter. Everyone is watching.
Sports day. The sack race starts now. The sack is itchy and smells of potatoes. The whistle goes.
Egg and spoon race. Your egg looks fragile. It is real and raw. The spoon is tiny. The finish is far.
You're invited to your first sleepover. A whole night at someone else's house. Their cereal. Their dark.
Someone at the sleepover starts a ghost story. Torch under the chin. Something creaks upstairs.
It's your birthday party. Who's coming? Your parent has a pen, a list and a budget. You choose.
There's a clown at a friend's party. He looks tired. His balloon dog has a puncture. He sighs a lot.
Your aunt gives you socks for your birthday. Again. They have little ducks on them. She's watching you.
Someone shoves your face into your birthday cake. Icing in your nose and one eyebrow. Everyone laughs.
Your parent wants to take the training wheels off. They promise to hold the seat. Probably.
You scraped your knee badly at break. There's gravel in it. It stings. It's also kind of impressive.
Swimming lessons start. The deep end looks very deep. A rubber brick waits at the bottom.
A kid shares their crayons and says you're best friends now. They gave you the good blue one.
Your best friend is moving away. The van is outside. They're on your doorstep, trying not to cry.
You want a puppy more than anything. You saw one with a spot on its ear. Your parents say "we'll see".
You get to take the class hamster home for the weekend. He is called Professor. He is plotting.
Times tables test tomorrow. Sevens are the worst. Your parent says it's easy, then gets one wrong.
You are cast as a tree in the school play. No lines. Your costume is a brown sack and two branches.
A chore chart goes up. Your name is on dishes. Every night. The sink is already full of greasy plates.
Someone offers cookies for your apple. Two cookies, chocolate chip, still soft. Your apple is bruised.
You are certain something lives under your bed. You heard it breathing. The gap is pure black.
The science fair is next week. Half the class is making a volcano. The kitchen has vinegar and old bread.
Your parent offers to cut your hair at home. Kitchen scissors, a towel, one video watched. Very confident.
Last day of school. Everyone brings the teacher a gift. Mugs, flowers, a huge candle. Your hands are empty.
Snow day! School is closed. The street is white and silent. Your boots are waiting by the door.
You come home with one shoe. The other foot is a wet sock. Your parent is staring at your feet.
An old phone, handed down. Cracked screen, one bar of battery. The wallpaper is a blurry sandwich.
You get added to a group chat with forty people. It pings all night. Memes, fights, someone's cat.
A folded note lands on your desk: "do u like anyone". Someone two rows back is watching closely.
Your crush walks past. They nod. Just a nod. Friendly? Cool? At the person behind you? Your face burns.
School camp sign-up. Three nights in cabins, no parents. A lake, bunk beds, canoes. Form due Friday.
Camp, night one. Someone in your cabin says the woods are haunted. A branch scrapes the window.
Camp, night two. You miss your own bed more than expected. Someone is snoring like a tractor.
A friend leans over: "Do you... wear deodorant?" They look worried for you. Gym was before lunch.
Your trousers ended above your ankles overnight. Your socks are on show. Your knees ache at night.
Your parent sits you down for The Talk. They brought diagrams. They are sweating. It's labelled neatly.
Your two best friends stopped talking. Both want you on their side. Each saved you a seat at lunch.
You're allowed to walk to school alone for the first time. Your parent watches from the window. Badly hidden.
You get your own house key. On a lanyard. Around your neck. It's bright orange and bounces when you run.
Home alone for two hours. The house is very quiet. The fridge hums. Every room feels bigger.
You offer to make dinner. Nobody stops you. There's a recipe book, half an onion and one egg.
You can earn pocket money doing chores. Bins, dishes, the gross bit of the bathroom. Every job has a price.
A hot day. You could set up a drink stand on the corner. There are lemons and a folding table.
Your friend wants to film a dance video to post online. They have a ring light. They need a second dancer.
Your phone says you used it nine hours yesterday. More than you slept. It seems proud of it.
Sleepover game: truth or dare. The bottle spins and stops on you. The whole circle leans in.
A teacher calls you their best student. Out loud. In front of everyone. Thirty heads turn.
Someone offers you the answers to tomorrow's test. A crumpled page. They swear it's real.
You made the final of the class spelling contest. A hall, a microphone, a judge. Your mouth is dry.
A pimple appears on your nose the morning of class photos. Red, shiny, enormous. It has a heartbeat.
Your sibling wants to share your room for a month. They snore. They bring every toy they own.
You want a pet. You've made a slideshow. Twelve slides, charts, cute photos. Your parents fold their arms.
You want a bold new haircut. You saved a photo. The hairdresser looks at it, then at you, then at it.
Kids at the park dare you to jump the ramp on your bike. It's a plank on two bricks. Someone's filming.
Everyone's at a party you weren't invited to. You see the photos. Cake, balloons, a group hug.
A friend told you a secret. Now someone asks you about it. They know half. They just need a yes.
You ask for a lock on your bedroom door. Your sibling keeps walking in. So does your parent, with laundry.
You discover the library has a whole section for older kids. Thick books, dark covers, dragons.
Team tryouts after school. The coach has a clipboard. The older kids look huge. Your trainers squeak.
A grandparent wants a weekly video call. They hold the phone very close. You mostly see a nostril.
A goose has taken over the path to school. It is staring at you. It hisses. It fears nothing.
You've invented a new sport. It needs a ladder and a trampoline. The rules are on a napkin.
A rumour says you have a crush. It's even true. Half the class knows by lunch. Your crush has heard.
It's 3 a.m. and you just woke up. You soiled your diaper, and you're hungry. Your parents are snoring.
Everyone is waiting for your first word. Both parents lean in, mouthing their own names very slowly.
Dinner is broccoli. Again. Three little green trees, steaming. They say it makes you big. Lies.
The stairs gate is open. The stairs go up and up. The banister is shiny and smooth. Nobody is looking.
First day of school. A kid is crying by the door, holding a dinosaur lunchbox. Everyone walks past.
Your first friend invites you to a sleepover. They have bunk beds and a dog called Biscuit.
The test answers are sitting on the teacher's desk. The teacher stepped out. The page is face up.
Your friends dare you to climb the tallest tree in the park. The lake glitters nearby. Everyone watches.
You could cut your own hair. How hard can it be? Scissors, a mirror, a tutorial. The light is very honest.
